login.note: Email + password on THIS instance only. A Mastodon account is instance-local: credentials for another instance will not work here, and the operator must know which instance the identity lives on before the window opens. Some instances put an OAuth/SSO provider on this page instead; mastodon.social does not.

logout.note: Sign-out is a DELETE (Rails) on /auth/sign_out with a CSRF token — visiting that URL with GET does not log anyone out, it renders or redirects. Use the Preferences menu item in the web UI.

traps: The <script id="initial-state"> element is present on the SIGNED-OUT page too — verified on mastodon.social 4.8.0-alpha on 2026-09-12, where it carried "access_token": null and no "me". Gating on 'the initial-state element exists' reports every anonymous visitor as signed in.

Almost everything worth reading is readable with NO session: /api/v1/timelines/public, /api/v1/accounts/lookup, an account's statuses, the whole /explore surface. A feed that loads is therefore zero evidence of a session — only a 'who am I' endpoint or meta.me is.

/api/v1/accounts/verify_credentials answers 401 {"error":"The access token is invalid"} with no session (verified 2026-09-12) — it does NOT redirect and it does not 403. Any other endpoint's 200 must not be read as authentication.

The instance is the boundary. Cookies, the OAuth token in initial-state, the handle and the whole session are scoped to this host; being live on mastodon.social says nothing about any other instance, and the same person is a different account on each.

Mastodon rate-limits the API per token (documented default: a few hundred requests per 5 minutes, tighter for writes) and answers 429 with X-RateLimit-* headers. A throttled read comes back as a short or empty timeline rather than an obvious error, so a recipe must check the status and those headers before believing an empty feed.
notes: THIS FILE IS ONE INSTANCE. Mastodon is not a site, it is software: every instance is its own origin, its own accounts, its own cookies and its own rate limits, and mastodon.social is merely the biggest one. TO CLONE IT FOR ANOTHER INSTANCE: copy this file to sites/<that-host>.json and change `domain`, `home`, `login.url`, `logout.url/selector`, `auth.probe_url` and `read.fixture_url` — swap the host everywhere it appears. NOTHING in probe_js is host-specific (it reads #initial-state and fetches a relative /api/v1 path, and it reports the instance from meta.domain), so the probe copies over unchanged. Keep `status: "unverified"` in the copy: a probe verified on mastodon.social is not verified on an instance running a different Mastodon version or a fork (GoToSocial, Akkoma, Hometown and glitch-soc all speak the same API but do not all render the same initial-state). PROBE STRATEGY: (a) the site's own embedded state object, with (b) a credentialed who-am-I as a fallback for the handle only. The web UI bootstraps React from <script id="initial-state" type="application/json">, whose meta object carries `me` (the account id) and `access_token` (the OAuth token the UI itself uses). Both empty = signed out, verified against a real signed-out document. meta.me is only a numeric id, so when initial-state does not also carry the account record the probe asks /api/v1/accounts/verify_credentials with that token and takes `acct`/`username`; a 401/403 there means the embedded token is dead and IS a signed-out verdict, while a network/CORS failure is explicitly NOT allowed to flip the verdict. The probe never returns the token. WHAT A READ RECIPE SHOULD DO: use the REST API with the Bearer token lifted from initial-state's meta.access_token — GET /api/v1/timelines/home?limit=40 (home), /api/v1/notifications, /api/v1/accounts/verify_credentials then /api/v1/accounts/<id>/statuses. Paginate with the Link header (max_id/min_id), not by page number. For public reads no token is needed: /api/v1/timelines/public?local=true and /api/v2/search. WRITE: empty. POST /api/v1/statuses with an Idempotency-Key header is the documented publish path and would be a clean write verb, but nothing here has driven it, so it is not listed.
probe_checked: 2026-09-12: ran live in the fork and returned a clean signed_out verdict (no throw, no 'no verdict'). The signed-OUT path is proven; the signed-IN path is still a hypothesis.
